sections.title: Introduction to Classical Chinese II
sections.description: Continuation of Intro to Classical Chinese I, which is the only prerequisite for this course. Upon completion of Shadick, readings in a wide selection of texts with Chinese commentaries may be taken up. These readings are in part chosen to reflect student interest. This is the second half of a year-long course. Those who enroll must take both semesters.

sections.title: Introduction to Classical Chinese II
sections.description: This course, designed for both undergraduates and graduates, is a continuation of CHIN 1050/ EALC 3621/EALC 7621 "Introduction to Classical Chinese I." It offers an introduction to the basic vocabulary and grammar of written classical Chinese, so as to help students develop the ability to read a wide variety of classical styles and translate relevant texts accurately into English. This course will be taught in English. No knowledge of modern Chinese or Mandarin is presumed, but students are required to have passed CHIN 1050/EALC 3621/EALC 7621 "Introduction to Classical Chinese I" in order to enroll in this course. Undergraduates must enroll in this course as CHIN 1055 or EALC 3622; graduates must enroll in this course as EALC 7622.
